rules.title: AB 325: Common pricing algorithm ban (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software that uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices) as part of a conspiracy or combination to restrain trade. It is also unlawful to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term.
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal usar o distribuir un algoritmo de precios común (software que usa datos de competidores para recomendar o influir en precios) como parte de una conspiración o combinación para restringir el comercio. También es ilegal usarlo o distribuirlo si se coacciona a otra persona para que adopte el precio o término comercial recomendado.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person (not end consumers) using or distributing a common pricing algorithm for any product or service, including rental housing pricing software; not specific to housing.
rules.penalty: Violations of the Cartwright Act are punishable as a crime; the bill also lowers the pleading standard for antitrust complaints (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16756.1).
rules.caveat: General antitrust provision that is not housing-specific; effective date computed under the constitutional default (chaptered Oct. 6, 2025, no urgency clause). Penalty details come from the digest and are not fully set out in the operative text.
